OC - Wooden tractor made from mostly scrap wood.

Here's a simple wooden tractor that I made from some old pallets (chassis), floor boards(front wheels) and some salvaged house frame (Rear wheels)

The main construction is a through dovetail joint that continues on as the front of the tractor. Wheel arches (outer) were cut on the table saw at ~20 degree angle.

Here's a view from the front:

https://files.catbox.moe/4tncu2.jpg

The exhaust pipe is just some Tassie Oak dowels stuck together and ebonised with iron acetate. They're not quite as dark in real life as they look in the photo, but got pretty dark.
Do you hand-sand it or whittle or use power tools? Most of the woodworking I do is for a purpose but I think using scraps for toys is a good idea. Might do that as a hobby.

I generally hand sand. For the corners I break them with a plane, spoke shave or chisel first, then sand with 120 grit.

For flat surfaces I have a strip of 120 grit paper nailed top the end of my bench. Then I can use the flat surface of the bench. It's a bit like a linisher, but much more gentle. Can also round over end grain corners by rotating the piece as I drag out across the paper.

I generally avoid power sanding as it's a bit too aggressive.
